body:
## Codex Review

### Overview
This patch makes `preventBaseUIHandler()` consistently available at runtime across Base UI's shared prop-merge paths, including direct `useRenderElement()` props and first-position object inputs in `mergeProps()` / `mergePropsN()`. The current branch keeps that fix centralized in the shared merge logic, and the latest cleanup removes now-redundant workaround handlers that were only needed before the runtime fix existed.

### Findings
No blocking issues found in this patch.

#### 1. ℹ️ [Informational] Browser perf checks remain effectively flat overall, with only small route-level variance in focused opener tests

**Impact**: The change sits in shared event and render-prop plumbing, so even small regressions would fan out across many components. The main risk area is open and mount work in controls that rely heavily on shared trigger/merge paths.

**Evidence**: I compared the current PR head against the latest `master` tip in Chromium using static exports, fresh browser instances, alternating run order, and aggregated repeated runs. The existing high-volume docs stress routes remained in the same band as `master`, and a later `select-perf` rerun with 100 no-throttle samples came back effectively flat. Shorter throttled reruns showed some small variance, but the larger baseline rerun did not reproduce a meaningful regression.

Stress-route runs:

| Route | Ref | Mean (ms) | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | Std dev (ms) | Samples |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `/experiments/perf/non-popup-controls` | PR head | 101.14 | 101.00 | 109.00 | 4.67 | 397 |
| `/experiments/perf/non-popup-controls` | `master` | 101.49 | 101.20 | 110.50 | 5.29 | 392 |
| `/experiments/perf/contained-triggers` | PR head | 102.44 | 100.70 | 121.90 | 11.32 | 389 |
| `/experiments/perf/contained-triggers` | `master` | 103.87 | 104.90 | 125.60 | 12.34 | 389 |
| `/experiments/perf/detached-triggers` | PR head | 43.20 | 42.50 | 50.50 | 3.48 | 387 |
| `/experiments/perf/detached-triggers` | `master` | 42.58 | 41.30 | 51.00 | 4.46 | 395 |

Focused select opener reruns:

| Scenario | Ref | Mean (ms) | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | Std dev (ms) | Samples |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `select-perf` (100 samples, no slowdown) | PR head | 104.20 | 104.34 | 113.52 | 4.69 | 100 |
| `select-perf` (100 samples, no slowdown) | `master` | 105.20 | 105.38 | 114.53 | 4.73 | 100 |
| `select-perf` (30 samples, 4x slowdown) | PR head | 331.39 | 332.95 | 343.43 | 7.49 | 30 |
| `select-perf` (30 samples, 4x slowdown) | `master` | 325.10 | 325.62 | 332.94 | 7.96 | 30 |

**Recommendation**: This still looks like the right tradeoff to land. If follow-up perf work is needed, prefer targeted hot-path simplifications inside the shared merge path over broader runtime machinery or component-by-component typing audits.

### Confidence: 4/5
High confidence based on a full pass over the branch diff, focused regression coverage around the merge seed paths, fresh type/test verification, and repeated Chromium benchmarking against the latest `master` tip.

### Notes
- The branch has been rebased onto the latest `master` tip, and the review above reflects the rebased branch rather than the earlier pre-rebase snapshot.
- The latest cleanups remove two redundant workarounds: the `wrapEventHandler(ourHandler)` fallback in the `!theirHandler` merge branch, and the empty `onMouseDown` shim in `ComboboxChip` that had only been forcing chip events through the older merge path.

performed_via_github_app.description:
Publish incredibly high performance websites and applications right from GitHub. The Netlify platform connects your repositories to an all-in-one workflow for global CDN deployment, continuous integration, and automatic (and free) HTTPS. Each time you commit changes, Netlify builds your site, prerenders markup, and optimizes assets on dedicated build infrastructure. Easily create an entirely automated workflows for your web applications

## Features

### Push your site live, directly from GitHub
Deploy your site to an ultra-redundant global CDN that’s purpose built for serving pages and assets quickly and consistently.

### Automate deployment
Netlify’s built-in Continuous Deployment automatically runs your build commands and deploys the result whenever you push to your Git repository.

### Add a custom domain
Purchase domains and manage DNS zones and records right inside of Netlify.

### HTTPS is automatic
Your site will automatically be secured with a free TLS certificate from Let’s Encrypt.

### Deploy Previews
Netlify’s Deploy Previews streamlined your workflow by giving you a unique, permanent URL to check what your changes will be like in production whenever you submit a pull request.

### And a lot more!
Netlify includes solutions for forms, identity, and even custom functions powered by AWS Lambda. And all this functionality can be configured directly in your repo.
